Checkpoint-backed runtime opacity gate on frozen R009 windows passed 0/5 gates and degraded PSNR/L1/flicker/static ghost versus route0, matched-lifespan, and residual baselines.

M1 non-oracle residual-component local refinement produced checkpoint-backed Gaussian renders but passed 0/5 frozen windows on PSNR+L1, worsened mean PSNR by 1.5629 dB, worsened mean L1 by 0.004043 versus route0, and recovered negative oracle fraction.

M2 non-oracle boundary-gated micro-densification produced checkpoint-backed renders but passed only 2/5 strict all-baseline PSNR+L1 windows, improved mean PSNR by only 0.0569 dB and mean L1 by only 0.0000903 versus route0, and recovered less than 1 percent of the oracle upper bound.
R026 boundary support had near-zero frozen-crop coverage, so R027 failure rejects the tested support+training recipe but leaves good-support visibility-event mechanisms unresolved.
Monocular depth discontinuities may provide non-oracle occlusion/reveal support after R026 boundary masks missed frozen crop regions.

R029 route0 continuation worsened route0, while R030 oracle-support micro-densification also worsened route0 with 0/5 route0 PSNR+L1 wins. This rejects support-only continuation of the current posthoc micro-densification recipe.
R031 will test whether Depth Anything 3 support masks improve non-oracle occlusion/reveal support overlap versus R026 without using frozen crop labels as method input.
DA3 setup and 900-frame inference passed, but R031/R032/R033 support variants reached only 0.000030/0.002846/0.001253 mean frozen-crop coverage, far below R020 high-recall boxes at 0.491371.

Current DA3 depth-edge/confidence/mask/flow support fusion did not strongly localize frozen event crops; it should not be promoted into a rendered event-crop recovery claim without a changed training-loop mechanism.
